topic: only-cli (oc) Guide 2026: Turn Any Website into a CLI Tailored for AI Agents

key_points: Oficial site: oc fetches a page, distills it into compact text with numbered actions, lets an agent drive the site by number
Claims: 1,444 tokens for four real pages vs 65,372 raw HTML (45x); Reddit thread 477 vs 52,899 tokens; 500-token budget cap
Five commands (oc open, oc do, oc find, oc next, oc read, oc raw, oc <site> <verb>) + four flags (--budget --json --html --session --verbose)
Install: npm install -g @only-cli/oc; Node 20+, three runtime deps, no daemon/browser extension/per-site adapters
Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot via skills directory or plugin
Repo: Turn any website into a compact CLI tailored for AI agents; browse the web in hundreds of tokens, not tens of thousands
Stars 507, forks 31, MIT license, created 2026-08-18 (very new / fast-growing), OpenSSF Scorecard badge
Gets past blocks by impersonating a real browser (impers Chrome, falls back to Firefox, then native fetch)
clis/ ships tuned site shortcuts: oc hn item 4711, oc gh repo; oc sites lists all
Benchmarks (oc 0.5.1-0.5.3, Sep 2026): 118x fewer tokens than raw HTML across 14 real pages (9,466 vs 1,119,003); 17x fewer than Jina Reader, 54x fewer than Playwright MCP accessibility snapshot
The command line is the agent's native interface; a model reads/writes text and a CLI is the purest text-in/text-out surface
Positions CLIs as the preferred interface for AI agents over browsers/rendered pages
Estimate: $1-5B/yr spent industry-wide processing web markup no agent will use
75% of HTML is noise for agent consumption; avg 33,181 tokens/page raw HTML vs 8,301 tokens SOM structured
~400M user-action page fetches/day across major AI agents; ~24,900 wasted tokens each
Positions token-efficient web access as a serious cost problem (commercial angle)
Roughly 80% of token budget spent on HTML tags a model cannot use
Measured Cloudflare docs: 9,541 tokens raw HTML vs 1,678 cleaned markdown (82% reduction); blog post 16,180 vs 3,150
An agent fetching 50 pages/day faces ~35M tokens/month passing raw HTML
Alternatives: markdown.new (Cloudflare edge conversion), Jina Reader (r.jina.ai prefix)

stats.fact: only-cli (oc) compresses web pages to a compact numbered CLI view; claims 1,444 tokens for four real pages that cost 65,372 as raw HTML (~45x fewer).
A Reddit thread that was 52,899 tokens raw costs 477 tokens through oc.

GitHub benchmark (Sep 2026, oc 0.5.1-0.5.3): 118x fewer tokens than raw HTML across 14 real pages — 9,466 vs 1,119,003 tokens; 17x fewer than Jina Reader, 54x fewer than Playwright MCP accessibility snapshot.
only-cli repo has 507 stars and 31 forks, MIT licensed, created 2026-08-18 (rapid early traction).
oc render budget is hard-capped at 500 tokens; uses three runtime deps and Node 20+; no daemon or browser extension.
Industry estimate: 75% of HTML is noise for agent consumption; average raw page ≈33,181 tokens vs 8,301 tokens as structured content (SOM).
Estimated $1-5B per year spent processing web markup agents never use (~400M page fetches/day, ~24,900 wasted tokens each).
Markdown vs raw HTML typically cuts agent token cost ~80% (e.g., Cloudflare docs 9,541 → 1,678 tokens; blog 16,180 → 3,150).

angles: Token cost explosion: agents waste most of their budget on raw HTML markup; oc turns any website into a numbered CLI agents drive by number (the 'browse in tokens, not pages' hook).
Zero-setup ergonomics: npx @only-cli/oc runs with no install and teaches itself via --help and the actions: line, plus a one-line skill/plugin for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot.
Benchmark credibility: 118x token reduction vs raw HTML, and beats Jina Reader (17x) and Playwright MCP (54x) — a concrete comparative selling point.
Cost as a real problem: $1-5B/yr industry waste on unused markup makes token-efficient browsing a legitimate commercial/developer concern, not just a novelty.
Access/bot-block resilience: oc impersonates a real browser (impers) so it gets past blocks that stop naive fetchers on Reddit, LinkedIn, and other protected sites.

Practical how-to: install, wire one line into your agent's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md or skills dir, learn the five commands, use site shortcuts (oc hn, oc gh), and fall back to raw/native fetch when needed.
